subject: Post-call summary + next steps — dedicated capacity & isolation (Starlift)
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@starlift.ai>, procurement@starlift.ai
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-28T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call summary + next steps — dedicated capacity & isolation (Starlift)

Alex / Jenna / procurement team — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick written summary so we have alignment and clear next steps. I captured the items we discussed and what we'll action from Redwood's side.

Key pain points (from your team):
- Latency spikes during business hours affecting live recommendation flows (25% of requests seeing >600ms).
- Growing model size and context length (current models ~30B, exploring 64k context) that increases memory pressure.
- Regulatory/IP concerns: model inference must run in an isolated tenant with audit logs retained 12 months.

Starlift goals for this engagement:
- Predictable throughput during peak: sustain ~20 concurrent sessions with 512-token responses (~2k tokens/sec steady-state).
- Latency SLO: p50 < 150ms, p95 < 400ms for 512-token generation on reserved capacity.
- Isolation: dedicated GPU pool per environment (prod/staging) with network-level separation and KMS-backed keys.
- Operational: canary rollouts + automatic fallback to lower-cost model variant if latency or capacity issues occur.

Prelim dedicated capacity recommendation (ballpark — we'll firm this up with profiling data):
- Reserved pool: 4x A100-class equivalents for prod (pinned to the tenant), with a burst policy to 6 GPUs for 15-minute windows.
- Staging: 1x A100-equivalent reserved.
- KV/prefix caching enabled; recommend aggressive KV cache for hot shards to reduce token cost.
- Suggest quantized model variants for cost-sensitive reranking workloads.

SLA targets & metrics to include in draft agreement:
- Uptime: 99.9% monthly availability for the dedicated pool (with scheduled maintenance windows).
- Latency: p95 generation SLO as above; we will instrument and report at token-level in the console.
- Incident RTO: 1 hour for platform-level incidents with a 24x7 escalation path.

Attachments: I attached my call notes (starlift-dedicated-scan-notes.xlsx) and a short example runbook (redwood-dedicated-mop-example.pdf) to illustrate how we hand off operations.

Next steps (RACI):
- Redwood (Mina / Rishi): provide a firm capacity sizing and preliminary commercial tiers based on today's numbers by EOD 2026-07-29. (Action: Rishi)
- Starlift (Alex / Jenna): share any perf traces or request distribution samples and point us at procurement contact / PO template. (Action: Alex / Jenna)
- Schedule: technical deep-dive with Redwood infra + Starlift infra for capacity profiling — propose Tue 2026-07-30 or Wed 2026-07-31.

If that all looks right, I'll circulate a short SOW/term sheet and a reserved-capacity quote once Rishi confirms sizing.

Thanks — talk soon.

--
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Thanks, Mina — this aligns with what we discussed. A couple clarifications from our side:
- The p95 target is reasonable; our internal SLA asks for p99 as well, but we can start with p95 in the contract and add p99 as a monitoring target for the pilot.
- For burst policy: can you confirm how billing would work for short bursts beyond the reserved commit? We need clarity for procurement.

Procurement note: Jenna (cc) will own the PO process; attaching our PO template in a follow-up. Our legal/compliance team will want SOC2 evidence and the KMS/HSM integration details.

We can target the deep-dive on Tue 7/30 at 11:00am PT. I'll send a calendar invite after we lock it.

Appreciate the quick turnaround here.

Best,

Looping in a pricing sketch so Mina can include it in the EOD sizing doc. This is a preliminary internal->external friendly outline; we'll convert to full quote once we confirm profiling numbers from the deep-dive.

Reserved tiers (prelim):
- Tier A (Prod small): 4 reserved A100-equiv, 24/7 access, burst to 6 for 15m windows — baseline monthly commit $58,000 USD.
- Tier B (Prod medium): 6 reserved A100-equiv, burst to 8 — baseline monthly commit $84,000 USD.
- Dev/Staging: 1 reserved A100-equiv — $6,500 USD/month.

Notes:
- Burst usage billed at a short-burst rate per GPU-minute; we can cap monthly burst spend per account to limit unknowns.
- Isolation premium (tenant-level isolation + dedicated network + KMS integration) carries a one-time onboarding fee and 8% uplift on monthly commit.
- SLAs and reporting: standard 99.9% availability; optional 4x faster response SLA available on enterprise contracts.

Mina — I'll attach the draft term sheet to the HubSpot deal once you approve the language.
